headline: High-risk filesystem and network-capable OpenHands paired with a non-runnable sample repo creates moderate prompt-injection and data-handling exposure, but no direct documented interaction pathway.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenHands can read/write the runtime filesystem and use MCP, so if spring-integration-samples content is mounted into the same workspace or copied into OpenHands, prompt-like content could be treated as instructions. The sample repo itself is not runnable and exposes no agent behavior, so the pathway is inferred rather than documented.
conditions: IF spring-integration-samples files are mounted into OpenHands' runtime workspace
IF OpenHands parses repository text as instructions or tool directives
mitigations: Keep the sample repo read-only and outside OpenHands' workspace
Disable MCP servers for the session
Use a separate staging copy for any file ingestion
Add a manual review step before acting on repository text

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenHands touches mounted files and handles model-provider API keys, while spring-integration-samples is a non-runnable open-source repo with no declared sensitive data classes. The pair can leak file contents only if the repo is placed in OpenHands' mounted volume; blast radius appears limited to local files, not a documented sensitive dataset.
conditions: IF sensitive files are mounted alongside spring-integration-samples in OpenHands
IF OpenHands forwards mounted file contents to its model provider during analysis
mitigations: Do not mount secrets into the OpenHands runtime
Use a dedicated workspace for the sample repo
Rotate any API keys used in the session after testing
Restrict outbound network access during review

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenHands has broad write and git-modification capability, but spring-integration-samples is marked runnable:false and has no write or concurrency surface. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; the only plausible conflict is if both are pointed at the same mounted volume or git checkout.
conditions: IF both agents are given the same writable checkout or mounted volume
IF spring-integration-samples is edited by an external process while OpenHands is active
mitigations: Avoid concurrent edits to the same checkout
Use git status checks before committing

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenHands can generate code or analysis from repository contents, but spring-integration-samples has no documented downstream action-taking authority. Without a second agent that executes OpenHands' output, the main risk is mistaken reliance on generated text rather than an automated harmful cascade.
conditions: IF OpenHands output is copied into another workflow without review
IF a downstream system treats OpenHands' repository analysis as authoritative
mitigations: Require human review before reuse of outputs
Add a verification checklist for any derived claims

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class, residency mismatch, or retention policy is documented for spring-integration-samples, and OpenHands only lists mounted runtime files and model-provider keys. With no PHI, EU PII, or regulated data flow shown, a compliance breach pathway is not evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data is later mounted into OpenHands
IF the sample repo is repurposed to store sensitive records
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the runtime
